To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the use of agar contact plates is a simple, effective and inexpensive method for monitoring the hygiene status of food-contact surfaces; (ii) the use of alginate swabs is a useful alternative to contact plates for monitoring the hygiene of surfaces, although it is more laborious and expensive; and (iii) the use of contact plates is the preferred method for assessing cleaning efficiency, although repeated sampling is necessary to assess the effectiveness of a cleaning regime.

agar contact plates were as good as, or better than, alginate swabs in detecting microorganisms on food contact surfaces, and that scrubbing with a brush is the best way to clean surfaces that are difficult to clean.

agar-contact plates are more convenient to use than alginate-swabbing and that the latter is at least as sensitive; that repeated sampling in selected premises showed some surfaces to be particularly difficult to clean; that scrubbing with a brush was the most effective cleaning method for these surfaces; and that other surfaces were more easily cleanable, and generally the new methods introduced as part the study were better than those originally used in the premises.
In summary, our research is concerned with
food hygiene in premises where high-risk foods are prepared and sold, such as fish and chip shops and take-away restaurants.
methods of sampling and cleaning food-contact surfaces in the food trade, and with the development of cleaning methods that are both effective and acceptable.
the development of a method for the microbiological examination of surfaces in food premises.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best method of cleaning food-contact surfaces is to scrub them with a nylon brush and a detergent and hypchlorite solution, followed by rinsing with hot water, and then drying with a clean cloth.
cleaning and disinfection of food-contact surfaces is a complex process, and no simple statement can be made about the best methods for any given set of surfaces.
the cleaning methods used in the premises were not satisfactory, and that there was scope for improvement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most effective way of cleaning food-contact surfaces was to use a multiuse cloth soaked in a detergent and a hypochlorite cleaning solution.
the use of a detergent and hypohlorite solution is the best method for cleaning food-contact surfaces, and the use of contact plates is the best method of sampling these surfaces.

the use of a detergent and hypchlorite solution, applied by scrubbing with a multiuse nylon brush and rinsing with water is the most effective method of cleaning surfaces in premises preparing or selling high-risk foods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is not possible to clean all food contact surfaces to an acceptable standard.
the cleaning of food-contact surfaces is not a trivial matter, and that cleaning is a process rather than a single event.
the cleaning methods used in food premises should be assessed and improved if necessary.
